verification.note: I traced this through the code and it holds. At backend/app/services/scanner.py:217-227, _is_flattened_transparent_picture returns False when another row on the drive has the same thumbnail_path. When that happens, the elif chain at scanner.py:514 falls through to scanner.py:526, which calls _is_letterboxed_image_thumbnail. That function returns True for a picture whose stored size is not 16:9 and whose stored thumbnail is 320x180 (scanner.py:177-189). The branch then calls write_thumbnail_atomically(gen_fn, ...) on the shared expected_thumb (scanner.py:536-538). gen_fn comes from get_thumbnail_generator, which returns generate_image_thumbnail for images (thumbnail.py:624-625). At thumbnail.py:483-486 that function now writes WebP whenever carries_transparency(source) is true. So a transparent logo.png that shares its slot with logo.jpg, where the slot still holds a letterboxed JPEG, gets a WebP written into the shared slot. That breaks I11. The guard does not cover this path. Before this change the letterbox branch also rewrote shared slots, but with a JPEG. Writing WebP from that path is new in this change.

specification_compliance: I11 is broken on the letterbox path. The shared-slot guard covers only the transparency branch and does not cover the letterbox branch that follows it (scanner.py:526-539).
potential_unspecified_behavior: Before this change, the letterbox branch already rewrote a shared stem slot with a JPEG made from whichever row was scanned. That is pre-existing behaviour, and I11 does not explicitly cover it.
regression_risks: In a shared stem slot, a WebP made from the transparent sibling can replace the thumbnail shown for the JPEG sibling (logo.jpg).
test_coverage: I did not check whether any test covers a shared slot combined with a letterboxed stored thumbnail on a transparent source.
not_verified: I did not run any test or scan; I checked the code only by reading it.
I did not open the backend tests to look for a shared-slot letterbox case.
I did not check how write_thumbnail_atomically behaves, or the ETag effects on Markdown projections.
